pr.title: Render summary pages in standards mode at the device's width
pr.head: 8240b5d24e003b029acf66585c7a81c3d6f3e158

summary: A summary page is the guided review page Projector builds for a pull request, like this one. The same function, page() in src/projector/site/__init__.py, writes the page in two places: the review pages the Projector site serves at reviews/<number>/ and reviews/<number>/<head>/, and the standalone page that project site page writes to disk.
Until now that page started with its <title>. It had no <!doctype html> line and no viewport meta tag, though the site's home page has both. That caused two problems:

• Quirks mode. A page with no doctype is laid out in quirks mode, the browser's mode for very old pages. In quirks mode a <form> gets a bottom margin, so the site bar's search box sat high and the bar was 10 to 15 pixels taller than on the site's other pages.
  • Desktop width on phones. Without a viewport meta tag, a phone lays the page out as if its screen were desktop width and then shrinks it. The narrow-screen rules in summary.css never applied.

The fix adds the doctype, charset and viewport lines to the top of page(), the same three lines home_page() starts with. Standards mode also changes two line heights slightly, which the pull request keeps on purpose: overview tables inherit the body's 1.55 line height, and a line holding only a link or inline code is as tall as the text around it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review, at 8240b5d: clean, with no finding threads.
  • One suggestion: page() and home_page() now repeat the same three opening lines, which a shared constant could hold.
  • The repository's gate passed at this head: 455 tests, project check, both plugin validations and git diff --check.

groups.title: The summary page's opening lines
groups.kicker: One function now opens every summary page in standards mode
intro: page() returns a summary page's HTML as one string. The change puts <!doctype html> first, keeps the charset line second, adds the viewport line, and moves the <title> below them. Everything after the title is unchanged.

Every summary page goes through page(): write_page calls it for the standalone page, and the site build calls it for each head's page and each pull request's newest-head page. So one edit covers all three.

files.note: The four new opening lines of the string page() returns.

checks.text: These three lines match the start of home_page(), character for character, read in the file at this head.

Nothing in src/ expects a summary page to start with <title>. The one title parser, page_title, reads repository pages under content/ with re.search, so the title's position does not matter to it. Checked by searching src/ for <title.

groups.title: Tests that pin the opening lines
groups.kicker: Three checks that every built page opens with the doctype and viewport
intro: Both test files define the same STANDARDS_HEAD constant, the three opening lines, and check that pages start with it. The test modules in this repository share no helpers, so each keeps its own copy.

tests/test_site.py adds a test that builds a site with one published summary, then reads every HTML file the build writes outside content/. That includes the home page shell, 404.html and both review pages. Pages under content/ are the repository's own files, copied as they are, so the test leaves them out. tests/test_summary.py updates two existing tests to check the standalone page and the review pages.

checks.text: With src/projector/site/__init__.py reverted to the base, all three tests fail and name each page's first line, such as <title>Core Summary</title>. At this head they pass. Checked by running the three tests against the base copy of the module.
